title: Quality-weighted soft-fuse with geo-steering and staged safe fallbacks
creator: Maya Chen
description: Design and implement a per-entity (dependency/model/tenant) 'soft-fuse' circuit that trips based on a composite quality score (latency, error-rate, and model-response-quality signal) and automatically triggers a staged, safe fallback choreography with geo-aware reroute options. Goal: reduce outage blast radius while preserving perceived availability and minimizing quality regressions for paying customers. The fuse should be SLO-aware (use SLO slack to adapt sensitivity), support gradual tripping (95%-to-100% trip window), and expose observability and debugging hooks for on-call and SRE teams.
acceptance_criteria: Per-entity circuit policies can be defined and updated via the policy store UI and API
Composite quality score computed in runtime for each request path and emitted as metric (quality.score)
Circuit trips when score falls below threshold adjusted by SLO slack and regional capacity, with configurable ramp windows
On tripped circuit: execute predefined fallback chain (1. prefix cache -> 2. quantized cheaper variant -> 3. regional reroute with warm cache -> 4. degrade response with structured warning)
No customer request receives a 500 solely due to the new soft-fuse behavior during gradual rollout (canary limits enforced)
Comprehensive dashboards and alerting exist: trip-rate, time-to-trip, fallback-hit-rate, restored-quality, and per-tenant cost delta
E2E chaos test (regional outage + traffic spike) demonstrates safe failover with degraded-but-serving behavior under controlled conditions
implementation_notes: Compute composite score as weighted combination: latency_pctl(95) normalized + error_rate windowed(1m) + eval-quality-signal(snapshot-based), weights configurable per-tenant
Use SLO controller output (per-tenant SLO slack) to automatically scale trip sensitivity; e.g., if slack < 5%, lower threshold to favor availability
Implement soft-fuse state machine with states OPEN, WARMING, SOFT_TRIPPED, HARD_TRIPPED, and RECOVERING. WARMING window implements probabilistic shed before full trip
Fallback chain orchestrated by router middleware; each step attaches structured metadata to response headers and emits fallback.step metric
Geo-steering integrates with existing Route Orchestrator; warm cache prefetch to target region on first detection of capacity imbalance
Policy store schema extended with 'quality_weights', 'trip_ramp_ms', 'regional_steward_priority', and 'fallback_chain'
rollout_plan: Start with internal tenants in us-west (10% sample) for 48h, monitor key metrics
Canary 1: select small set of low-latency paying tenants across 2 regions (5% traffic), 72h
Canary 2: expand to 25% of tenants with staged ramp over 7 days, run chaos test day 3
Global rollout contingent on: <5% increase in latencies for unaffected tenants, fallback hit-rate < 3% for P0 customers, no unhandled 5xx events
observability: Emit metrics: quality.score, circuit.state, fallback.step, fallback.latency_penalty, trip_latency_pctl
Dashboards: per-tenant heatmap of quality.score, regional capacity vs trips, fallback chain waterfall
Pager thresholds: trip-rate > 1% sustained for 5m for top-100 tenants triggers SEV2 investigation
testing_plan: Unit tests for score computation, policy parsing, and state transitions
Integration tests: router middleware invokes fallback chain end-to-end with mocked downstreams
Load tests: synthetic workload with modeled latency and error spikes to validate ramp behavior
Chaos tests: simulate regional network partition and downstream model OOM to verify geo-steer and warm cache actions
Security review for policy API and privilege separation before canary
